Q: How to find d, given p, q, and e in RSA? A:

I think it's easier to visualize in a tabular format than over verbosity (both inputs are primes so an inverse definitely exists) :

r := remainder

t := quotient


        (old) t   (new) t   (new) r  (old) r    oT x nR      oR x nT  oTnR - oRnT

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1           1         -3    271412  [2490599]    271412     -7471797   [7743209]
2          -3         28     47891    271412    -143673      7599536   -7743209

3          28       -143     31957     47891     894796     -6848413    7743209
4        -143        171     15934     31957   -2278562      5464647   -7743209

5         171       -485        89     15934      15219     -7727990    7743209
6        -485      86986         3        89      -1455      7741754   -7743209

7       86986   -2523079         2         3     173972     -7569237    7743209
8    -2523079   [2610065]        1         2   -2523079      5220130   -7743209

                 2610065 := 2490599^-1 (mod 7743209)

First thing that jumps out as an invariant is the right most column of

old-quotient x new-remainder - old-remainder x new quotient

Because its absolute value always matches original modulus, with alternating signs. In fact, every column other than the new and old remainders exhibit sign alternation. You can potentially even end the looping 1 cycle sooner :

old-quotient(row7) - new-quotient(row7)

 2610065 = (86986) - (-2523079)

Q: Htaccess rewriting rule for localhost A: 
RewriteRule https://www.sanatariol.com(.+)\.html$ index.php?_htaccess_url=$1&%{QUERY_STRING} [L]

The RewriteRule directive matches against the URL-path only (not the absolute URL). So, the above rule will not match.

Try the following instead:

RewriteRule (.+)\.html$ index.php?_htaccess_url=$1 [QSA,L]

You also don't need to manually append the query string, use the QSA (Query String Append) flag instead.

Q: How do I use the Windows API to determine if NUMA is enabled? A:

I had a bug in my code. I was using the same variable for the return value and the out parameter, so my function was returning true, not the highest NUMA node number. I've fixed the bug and now I'm getting back 0, as expected.

Q: Converting Intersystems cache objectscript into a python function A:

intersys.pythonbind3 doesn't give you a %ResultSet-shaped wrapper directly. You have to instantiate the object via run_class_method, then wrap the returned oref as a database_object so you can call instance method on it. So:

import intersys.pythonbind3

conn = intersys.pythonbind3.connection()
conn.connect_now("host:port:NAMESPACE", "user", "password", None)
database = intersys.pythonbind3.database(conn)

# equivalent of: s Rset=##class(%ResultSet).%New("%SYSTEM.License.UserListAll")
oref = database.run_class_method("%ResultSet", "%New", ["%SYSTEM.License.UserListAll"])
rset = intersys.pythonbind3.database_object(database, oref)

# s r=Rset.Execute()
rset.invoke_method("Execute", [])

# s ncol=Rset.GetColumnCount()
ncol = rset.invoke_method("GetColumnCount", [])

# While (Rset.Next()) {f i=1:1:ncol w !,Rset.GetData(i)}
while rset.invoke_method("Next", []):
    for i in range(1, ncol + 1):
        print(rset.invoke_method("GetData", [i]))

Generally run_class_method(class, method, args) is for calling classmethod (like %New, which just returns an oref as an int), and once you have an oref you wrap it with database_object(database, oref) so you can call instance methods on it via nvoke_method(name, args). Every method call in your ObjecScript maps 1:1 to an invoke_method call once you're holding the wrapped object.

Q: Reloading .env variables without restarting server (Laravel 5, shared hosting) A:

For Laravel applications using configuration caching, restarting PHP itself is usually not the relevant part.

If `php artisan config:cache` has previously been executed, Laravel will keep using the generated `bootstrap/cache/config.php`. Updating `.env` does not automatically regenerate that file.

The normal solution is:

php artisan config:clear

php artisan config:cache

The difficult case is shared hosting where you may only have FTP access and cannot reliably execute Artisan after every deployment.

I maintain a package for that specific situation:

https://github.com/Codegenie-BE/laravel-config-cache-guard

It checks whether the deployed Laravel config cache still matches the current configuration sources before the application boots and can automatically invalidate/repair a stale cache.

It also works without depending on shell `exec()` access, which is useful on restrictive shared-hosting environments.

Disclosure: I maintain the package.

Q: Git clone over SSH hangs in WSL2 at expecting SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY A:

It stalls at SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY because that is the first large inbound packet, carrying the host key and signature. PowerShell works because the Windows stack has black hole detection. HTTPS works because TLS records are smaller.

Quick way to confirm, force a smaller host key so the reply fits:

ssh -T -o HostKeyAlgorithms=ssh-ed25519 -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=ssh-ed25519 git@github.com

If that connects, it's packet size. Forcing curve25519-sha256 earlier wouldn't have helped either. In WSL try:

sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400

And add it to /etc/wsl.conf :

[boot]
command = ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400

MSS clamping is the cleaner fix, but make sure you run wsl --shutdown between attempts:

sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN \
  -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1452
